records.label: spacr.ml.regression#28
records.source: ``'long'`` keeps one fitted row per well-guide pair. At gene level, each row carries all retained measured gene fractions of that complete well; guide-level fits retain the guide interaction. Gene-level LONG horseshoe fits weight only observation log likelihood by inverse fitted-row multiplicity per complete well, so each well contributes once without rescaling counts, exposures, design standardization or priors. ``'wide'`` pivots fractions to one row per independent well before fitting. Full gene compositions can confound a common coefficient shift with the intercept; existing estimator priors and coefficient units are retained. Mixed models keep their long nesting representation even when a wide count input was supplied.
records.context: ``'long'`` keeps one fitted row per well-guide pair. At gene level, each row carries all retained measured gene fractions of that complete well; guide-level fits retain the guide interaction. Gene-level LONG horseshoe fits weight only observation log likelihood by inverse fitted-row multiplicity per complete well, so each well contributes once without rescaling counts, exposures, design standardization or priors. ``'wide'`` pivots fractions to one row per independent well before fitting. Full gene compositions can confound a common coefficient shift with the intercept; existing estimator priors and coefficient units are retained. Mixed models keep their long nesting representation even when a wide count input was supplied.
records.translation: ``'long'`` conserva una fila ajustada por cada par pocillo-guía. A nivel de gen, cada fila contiene todas las fracciones génicas medidas y conservadas de ese pocillo completamente identificado; los ajustes a nivel de guía conservan la interacción de guía. Los ajustes LONG de horseshoe a nivel de gen ponderan solo la log-verosimilitud de las observaciones por el inverso del número de filas ajustadas por pocillo completamente identificado, de modo que cada pocillo contribuye una vez sin reescalar recuentos, exposiciones, estandarización del diseño ni distribuciones previas. ``'wide'`` pivota las fracciones a una fila por pocillo independiente antes del ajuste. Las composiciones génicas completas pueden confundir un desplazamiento común de los coeficientes con el intercepto; se conservan las distribuciones previas y las unidades de los coeficientes del estimador existente. Los modelos mixtos conservan su representación anidada en formato largo incluso si los recuentos de entrada se proporcionaron en formato ancho.

records.label: spacr.ml.regression_model#28
records.source: Optional aligned observation log-likelihood weights for ``horseshoe``. Counts, exposures and design standardization are not rescaled. Automatic global-prior calibration counts identified nonconstant predictors and independent physical wells. Weighted rows require aligned complete well identities in ``X.attrs['likelihood_well_ids']``. For arbitrary weights, use ``spacr.power_model.ModelData`` with an explicit ``scale_global``.
records.context: Optional aligned observation log-likelihood weights for ``horseshoe``. Counts, exposures and design standardization are not rescaled. Automatic global-prior calibration counts identified nonconstant predictors and independent physical microplate sample positions. Weighted rows require aligned complete microplate sample position identities in ``X.attrs['likelihood_well_ids']``. For arbitrary weights, use ``spacr.power_model.ModelData`` with an explicit ``scale_global``.
records.translation: Pesos opcionales, alineados por fila, de la log-verosimilitud de las observaciones para ``horseshoe``. Los recuentos, las exposiciones y la estandarización del diseño no se reescalan. La calibración automática de la escala global previa cuenta los predictores identificados no constantes y los pocillos físicos independientes. Las filas ponderadas requieren identidades completas de pocillo alineadas en ``X.attrs['likelihood_well_ids']``. Para pesos arbitrarios, use ``spacr.power_model.ModelData`` con un ``scale_global`` explícito.

records.source: Ordinary designs have one row per well. Repeated LONG observations may retain all rows with inverse multiplicity likelihood weights; design centering and scaling still use the retained rows. Automatic prior calibration counts identified nonconstant predictors and independent physical wells established by explicit row-aligned identities.
records.context: Ordinary designs have one row per microplate sample position. Repeated LONG observations may retain all rows with inverse multiplicity likelihood weights; design centering and scaling still use the retained rows. Automatic prior calibration counts identified nonconstant predictors and independent physical microplate sample positions established by explicit row-aligned identities.
records.translation: Los diseños habituales tienen una fila por pocillo. Las observaciones LONG repetidas pueden conservar todas las filas con pesos de verosimilitud inversos a su multiplicidad; el centrado y el escalado del diseño siguen utilizando las filas conservadas. La calibración automática de las distribuciones previas cuenta los predictores identificados no constantes y los pocillos físicos independientes establecidos mediante identidades explícitas alineadas con las filas.

records.source: optional positive finite row weights applied only to the observation log likelihood. ``None`` counts every row once; inverse within-well multiplicities count repeated LONG rows once per well.

records.translation: pesos opcionales positivos y finitos por fila, aplicados solo a la log-verosimilitud de las observaciones. ``None`` cuenta cada fila una vez; los inversos de las multiplicidades dentro de cada pocillo cuentan las filas LONG repetidas una vez por pocillo.

records.label: spacr.power_model.ModelData#10
records.source: optional complete physical-well identities in design-row order. Automatic calibration of weighted rows requires these identities, exact repeated designs/counts/exposures within each well and inverse row-multiplicity weights. Arbitrary weights require an explicit global prior scale instead of an inferred independent-well count.
records.context: optional complete physical-microplate sample position identities in design-row order. Automatic calibration of weighted rows requires these identities, exact repeated designs/counts/exposures within each microplate sample position and inverse row-multiplicity weights. Arbitrary weights require an explicit global prior scale instead of an inferred independent-microplate sample position count.
records.translation: identidades completas opcionales de pocillos físicos en el orden de las filas del diseño. La calibración automática de filas ponderadas requiere estas identidades, diseños/recuentos/exposiciones repetidos exactamente dentro de cada pocillo y pesos inversos a la multiplicidad de filas. Los pesos arbitrarios requieren una escala global previa explícita en lugar de inferir el número de pocillos independientes.

records.label: spacr.power_model.fit_model#6
records.source: prior guess at the number of true hits, used for the horseshoe's global scale. Default: 5 % of identified nonconstant predictors, floored at one. It must be strictly between zero and the identified predictor count. With one identified predictor, provide an explicit valid expected-hit count or ``scale_global``; a design with no identified predictor is refused.
records.context: prior guess at the number of true hits, used for the horseshoe's global scale. Default: 5 % of identified nonconstant predictors, floored at one. It must be strictly between zero and the identified predictor count. With one identified predictor, provide an explicit valid expected-hit count or ``scale_global``; a design with no identified predictor is refused.
records.translation: suposición previa del número de aciertos reales, utilizada para la escala global de horseshoe. Valor predeterminado: el 5 % de los predictores identificados no constantes, con un mínimo de uno. Debe estar estrictamente entre cero y el número de predictores identificados. Con un predictor identificado, proporcione explícitamente un número esperado de aciertos válido o ``scale_global``; se rechaza un diseño sin predictores identificados.
